package apps

import kyo.*
import kyo.UI.*
import tui4s.kyoui.Tui

/** The Counter in plain kyo-ui: only kyo-ui's API, plus `Tui.quit` for the quit key. */
object Counter:

    val app: UI < Sync =
        for count <- Signal.initRef(0)
        yield div.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('+'), _, _) => count.updateAndGet(_ + 1)
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('-'), _, _) => count.updateAndGet(_ - 1)
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('q'), _, _) => Tui.quit
            case _                                       => ()
        }(
            h1("Counter"),
            span("Count: ", count.map(_.toString)).id("count"),
            div.style(_.row.gap(1.px))(
                button("+").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ + 1)),
                button("-").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ - 1))
            ),
            p("+ / - change it, Tab moves, Enter presses, q quits").style(_.color(Style.Color.gray))
        )

    /** One counter as a function: its state is allocated when the function runs. */
    def counter(label: String): UI < Sync =
        for count <- Signal.initRef(0)
        yield div.style(_.border(1.px, Style.Color.slate).padding(0.px, 1.px))(
            span(label).style(_.bold),
            span("Count: ", count.map(_.toString)),
            div.style(_.row.gap(1.px))(
                button("+").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ + 1)),
                button("-").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ - 1))
            )
        )

    /** Two independent counters side by side. */
    val twoCounters: UI < Sync =
        for
            left  <- counter("Left")
            right <- counter("Right")
        yield div.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('q'), _, _) => Tui.quit
            case _                                       => ()
        }(
            h1("Two counters"),
            div.style(_.row.gap(2.px))(left, right),
            p("Tab moves between the four buttons, Enter presses, q quits").style(_.color(Style.Color.gray))
        )
end Counter

object CounterMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(Counter.app))

object TwoCountersMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(Counter.twoCounters))

object CounterHooksMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(CounterHooks.app))

object CounterHooksDynamicMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(CounterHooks.dynamic))

import java.io.IOException
import java.nio.file.Files
import java.nio.file.Path
import kyo.*
import scala.jdk.CollectionConverters.*
import tui4s.*

enum Pane derives CanEqual:
    case Input, Items

final case class Item(title: String, done: Boolean = false) derives CanEqual

final case class Todo(
    field: TextField = TextField.empty,
    items: Vector[Item] = Vector.empty,
    selected: Int = 0,
    focus: Focus[Pane] = Focus(Pane.Input, Pane.Items),
    ready: Boolean = false,
    status: String = "loading…",
) derives CanEqual:
    def left: Int = items.count(!_.done)

    def add: Todo =
      if field.isBlank then this
      else
          copy(
            field = TextField.empty,
            items = items :+ Item(field.text.trim),
            selected = items.size,
          )

    def move(by: Int): Todo =
      copy(selected = (selected + by).max(0).min((items.size - 1).max(0)))

    def toggle: Todo =
      if items.isEmpty then this
      else
          copy(items =
            items.updated(
              selected,
              items(selected).copy(done = !items(selected).done),
            ),
          )

    def delete: Todo =
      if items.isEmpty then this
      else
          val rest = items.patch(selected, Nil, 1)
          copy(items = rest, selected = selected.min((rest.size - 1).max(0)))

    def nextPane: Todo = copy(focus = focus.next)

    def typed(event: Event): Todo =
        val f = field.edit(event)
        // The same object when the key did nothing: no frame.
        if f eq field then this else copy(field = f)

    def loaded(r: Result[IOException, Vector[Item]]): Todo = r match
        case Result.Success(items) =>
          copy(items = items, ready = true, status = s"${items.size} loaded")
        case failed                =>
          copy(ready = true, status = s"could not load: $failed")

    def saved(r: Result[IOException, Unit]): Todo = r match
        case Result.Success(_) => copy(status = "saved")
        case failed            => copy(status = s"could not save: $failed")
end Todo

      bind(Key.Ctrl('s'), "save")(save),
      bind(Key.Esc, "quit")(_ => Quit),
    )

    val inputKeys: Keymap[Todo] =
      Keymap(bind(Key.Enter, "add")(_.add)) ++ global

    val itemKeys: Keymap[Todo] = Keymap(
      bind(Key.Up, "up")(_.move(-1)).or('k'),
      bind(Key.Down, "down")(_.move(1)).or('j'),
      bind(' ', "toggle")(_.toggle),
      bind('d', "delete")(_.delete),
      bind('q', "quit")(_ => Quit),
    ) ++ global

      if t.focus.is(Pane.Input) then inputKeys else itemKeys

    def init: Todo = Todo()

    /** Load once at start: the initial state declares the task; its fold sets
      * `ready`, which removes it.

      else

      * the result. With an id, a second Ctrl-S replaces a save that is still
      * running (latest wins).
      */
    private def save(t: Todo): Next[Todo] =
      t.copy(status = "saving…")
        .withTask(
          source
            .task(Abort.run[IOException](TodoStore.save(t.items)))(_.saved(_))
            .id("save"),
        )

    def update(t: Todo, event: Event): Next[Todo] =
        val active = keys(t)
        event match
            case active(action)              => action(t)
            // The rest is text: 'q' and 'd' type letters here.
            case e if t.focus.is(Pane.Input) => t.typed(e)
            case _                           => t

    def view(t: Todo): View =
        val inInput = t.focus.is(Pane.Input)
        column(
          input(t.field, focused = inInput, placeholder = "What needs doing?")
            .bordered(" New ", focused = inInput)
            .size(3),
          list(t.items.map(itemLine), t.selected, focused = !inInput)
            .bordered(s" Todo · ${t.left} left ", focused = !inInput),
          row(help(keys(t)), text(t.status.dim).right.size(24)).size(1),
        )
    end view

    private def itemLine(item: Item): Line =
      if item.done then line("✔ ".green, item.title.dim.crossedOut)
      else line("☐ ", item.title)
end TodoApp

package examples.ziodashboard

import tui4s.interop.zio.*
import zio.*
import zio.stream.ZStream

final case class Dash(
    tab: Int = 0,
    cpu: Double = 0.0,
    history: Vector[Long] = Vector.empty,
    logs: Vector[String] = Vector.empty,
    paused: Boolean = false,
) derives CanEqual:
    def sample(v: Double): Dash  =
      copy(cpu = v, history = (history :+ (v * 100).toLong).takeRight(200))
    def log(line: String): Dash  = copy(logs = (logs :+ line).takeRight(500))
    def switchTab(by: Int): Dash =
      copy(tab = Math.floorMod(tab + by, Dash.tabs.size))
    def togglePause: Dash        = copy(paused = !paused)
end Dash

object Dash:
    val tabs: Vector[String] = Vector("Metrics", "Requests")

/** The Dashboard for ZIO users (SPEC 3.4): tabs, a gauge and a sparkline fed by
  * a ZIO poller every 250 ms, and a log pane fed by a `ZStream`. No Kyo type:
  * `ZStream`, `Schedule`, `Random` and `700.millis` are ZIO's.
  *
  * Run it: `sbt examples/launchers`, then `examples/target/bin/ziodashboard`.
  */
object DashboardApp extends TuiApp[Dash]:
    val requests: ZStream[Any, Nothing, String] =
      ZStream
        .iterate(1)(_ + 1)
        .schedule(Schedule.spaced(700.millis))
        .map(i => s"GET /api/items/$i 200")

    val keys: Keymap[Dash] = Keymap(
      bind(Key.Left, "prev tab")(_.switchTab(-1)),
      bind(Key.Right, "next tab")(_.switchTab(1)),
      bind('p', "pause")(_.togglePause),
      bind('q', "quit")(_ => Quit),
    )

    def init: Dash = Dash()

    def update(d: Dash, event: Event): Next[Dash] = keys(d, event)

    /** A function of the state: pausing removes the poller, so its ZIO is
      * interrupted; the log stream keeps running.
      */
    override def sources(d: Dash): Seq[Source[Dash]] =
        val logs = source.stream(requests)(_.log(_)).id("logs")
        val cpu  =
          source.poll(250.millis)(Random.nextDouble)(_.sample(_)).id("cpu")
        if d.paused then Seq(logs) else Seq(logs, cpu)

    def view(d: Dash): View =
      column(
        tabs(Dash.tabs, d.tab).bordered(" Dashboard ").size(3),
        if d.tab == 0 then metrics(d)
        else logPane(d.logs).bordered(" Requests "),
        help(keys).size(1),
      )

    private def metrics(d: Dash): View =
      row(
        column(
          gauge(d.cpu, f"${d.cpu * 100}%.0f%%")
            .bordered(if d.paused then " CPU (paused) " else " CPU ")
            .size(3),
          sparkline(d.history, max = Some(100L)).bordered(" History "),
        ).percent(60),
        logPane(d.logs).bordered(" Requests "),
      )
end DashboardApp

## Differences that matter for the decision

Facts only. Each item names its evidence.

1. What the user writes.
   - Current core: one immutable state, `update(state, event): Next[S]`, `view(state): View`, a `Keymap`, and
     `sources(state)` for background work. No component abstraction: the Counter has one number.
   - kyo-ui runner: UI values with signals. State is one or more Kyo refs. Handlers write the refs. A component is a
     function (hooks) or a `Component` subclass. Two independent counters are two calls (`counter("Left")`,
     `counter("Right")`) or two values (`CounterBox("Left")`, `CounterBox("Right")`).
   - Facades: the same kyo-ui model with ZIO or `F[_]` values in the handlers and in the hooks.
2. Effect types in the user's code.
   - Current core Counter (all three ecosystems): no effect type. The Todo and Dashboard of the core use Kyo types
     (`Sync`, `Abort`, `Stream`, `Async`) only for background work.
   - kyo-ui runner: Kyo types in every app, also in the Counter (`UI < Sync`, `SignalRef`, `KyoApp`), and handlers
     typed `Any < Async`.
   - Facades: no Kyo import and no Kyo effect type. Kyo DATA types stay reachable through aliases (facades REPORT
     O2).
3. Where state lives and who owns it.
   - Current core: one value in the engine. Each frame shows one state value.
   - kyo-ui runner: many refs. Hooks: made when the effect runs (top `for`) or at mount (`component(...)`).
     Component class: the runner makes one ref per instance at mount and keeps it by position and class.
   - Facades: refs from `useSignal` that are the same Kyo cell that kyo-ui binds. The facade `Component.mount`
     makes the ref when the app `for` runs; it is not kept by position in a runner.
4. How the screen changes.
   - Current core: the whole view is rebuilt and painted after each change; jatatui writes only the changed cells
     (RenderLoop.scala:181-185 @ feat/core-3-terminal).
   - kyo-ui runner: only the changed regions are repainted. One `+` writes 1 cell, 26 bytes (runner REPORT N4,
     N6). A settle step makes a frame wait for all consequences of an event; it is "very likely" glitch-free, not
     certain (N2). An exact fix needs a change in Kyo (runner REPORT, upstream proposal 1).
   - Latency numbers exist for both, from different machines: old core bench B4 p50 1.56 ms, p99 3.91 ms (macOS);
     runner Counter p50 0.63 ms, p99 1.24 ms (Linux container). The runner REPORT says that this is not a direct
     comparison.
5. Traps.
   - Current core: `Next[S]` is a union, so the result type of `update` must be written (App.scala:95); the Kyo
     `Stream.unfold` chunk size (DashboardApp.scala:30-31); the `fs2.*` import clash (Cats).
   - kyo-ui runner: the lift trap. A handler without the type `Any < Async` compiles and never runs, with no error
     and no warning (Todo.scala:85-94; runner REPORT O5; reproduced by the verifier).
   - Facades: the lift trap fails at compile time with a tui4s message (generated `compiletime.error` overloads).
     Cats only: a foreign `SignallingRef` in a binding setter fails at run time (O3).
6. Widgets and layout.
   - Current core: jatatui widgets (gauge, sparkline, tabs, list, table) through its own `View` DSL.
   - kyo-ui runner: kyo-ui HTML elements with flexbox layout in cells. No built-in gauge or sparkline (the Dashboard
     draws them as text). No scrolling, overlays, mouse or `onKeyUp`; 1 px = 1 cell (runner REPORT N7, N8).
7. Facade parity.
   - Old facades: the Counter text is the same in Kyo, ZIO and Cats except the package and the import (the branch
     also has `examples/src/parity/CounterBody.scala.txt` and `ParitySuite`). The old facades have no Todo.
   - New facades: the ZIO and Cats apps are near copies of each other. They are not the same text as the runner
     apps (other features, ids for the test runner, `update` instead of `updateAndGet`). The new facades have no
     Dashboard.
8. How far each variant was run.
   - Current core: CI green on PR 5 with a Linux terminal job; the macOS expect checklist passed 47/47 (HANDOFF).
     Old ZIO facade: 14 confirmed findings not fixed. Old Cats facade: review not started.
   - kyo-ui runner: headless tests and a real PTY run (Counter and Todo) green on this Linux machine (verifier).
     The Dashboard has no PTY run.
   - Facades: in the facades prototype, a headless test runner only (kyo-ui's own HTML renderer). The integration
     prototype (DONE) runs the unchanged ZIO and Cats Counter and Todo on the terminal runner's headless
     `TestBackend`: 6/6 and 6/6 in each of 3 runs, and a real PTY run of the ZIO and Cats Counter passes.
9. Coverage of the effect points (facades). Drag and drop has no ZIO or Cats form yet: 9 setters are skipped
   (facades REPORT O1). So "ZIO / F[_] types at every effect point" is not yet true.
10. Entry points.
   - Current core: `object X extends TuiApp[S]`. `TuiApp` is a Kyo main, a `ZIOAppDefault` (ZIO) or an
     `IOApp.Simple` (Cats).
   - kyo-ui runner: `object X extends KyoApp: run(Tui.run(app))`.
   - Facades (integration prototype): `object X extends ZIOAppDefault: def run = Tui.run(app)` or
     `object X extends IOApp.Simple: def run: IO[Unit] = Tui.run(app)`. To quit from a handler, ZIO uses the
     global `Tui.quit`; Cats uses the `F[Unit]` that `Tui.runWithQuit` gives to the app.
